ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an inverting operational amplifier low-pass filter circuit. The input Vi first passes through R1, labeled as 1 kΩ in the figure, and is connected to the inverting terminal of the op-amp; the non-inverting terminal is grounded. The output Vo is connected back to the inverting terminal through the feedback network. In the feedback network, R2 is located above, and the capacitor C is located below and labeled as 10 nF. The two are connected between the same pair of nodes, so R2 and C are connected in parallel in the feedback branch. Reasoning: The problem gives the cutoff frequency fc = 5 kHz and asks for the value of R2. The cutoff frequency of this first-order inverting active low-pass filter is determined by R2 and C in the feedback branch: fc = 1/(2πR2C). Therefore R2 = 1/(2πfcC). Substituting fc = 5000 Hz, C = 10 nF = 10e-9 F, gives R2 = 1/(2π × 5000 × 10e-9) Ω ≈ 3183 Ω = 3.18 kΩ.
